title: Does Asking for a Confidence Estimate Change the Answer? Observer-Effect on Honesty

original_idea.body: Observer-effect: does eliciting confidence/justification change the answer across three conditions.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Plausible chain (eval validity matters) but the link from observer-effect to reduced catastrophic risk has a gap.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Accessible: three prompt conditions, compare answer distributions; motivated beginner can run it.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Tightly scoped single experiment (3 conditions, flip rate) with clear success criteria.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Independent-friendly methodological check, public models, no lab incentive.

low_compute.reasoning: Pure inference, small models, free-tier feasible.

novelty.reasoning: Observer effects on elicitation plausibly untested directly though related introspection work exists.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Elicitation-induced observer effect on honesty may be an open angle.
